summary: Russian forces launched coordinated missile and drone strikes across multiple Ukrainian cities including Odesa, Poltava, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipro, causing casualties and infrastructure damage. Ukrainian special forces destroyed a Russian Su-24M bomber at an airfield in occupied Crimea using naval drones. Political instability intensified as Defense Minister Fedorov resigned, triggering nationwide protests and the resignation of the Deputy Air Force Commander.
key_points: Russian Kh-59 cruise missiles struck Odesa, with multiple impacts reported. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69103)
Shahed-type drones targeted Poltava city, with at least two guided jet-powered drones reported. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69110)
Ukrainian National Guard special forces destroyed a Russian Su-24M at Saky airfield in Crimea using FPV drones. (Source: @UkraineNow/82704)
Russian ballistic missile launches detected from Bryansk region, with four missiles reported. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69120)
Russian forces hit Zaporizhzhia with three KAB guided bombs, killing three people and damaging residential buildings. (Source: @UkraineNow/82703)
Russian strikes on Kharkiv, Odesa, and Dnipro killed at least two civilians and injured seven others. (Source: @UkraineNow/82706)
Defense Minister Fedorov resigned; protests erupted in Kyiv, Lviv, Dnipro, Poltava, Lutsk, and Zaporizhzhia demanding his return. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31662)
United Kingdom pledged €300 million for procurement of Swedish Gripen fighter jets for Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/82702)

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces launched coordinated missile and drone strikes across multiple Ukrainian cities including Odesa, Poltava, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipro, causing casualties and infrastructure damage. Ukrainian special forces destroyed a Russian Su-24M bomber at an airfield in occupied Crimea using naval drones. Political instability intensified as Defense Minister Fedorov resigned, triggering nationwide protests and the resignation of the Deputy Air Force Commander.

points: Ukrainian National Guard Omega special forces conducted a successful operation destroying a Russian Su-24M bomber at Saky airfield in occupied Crimea, with two FPV drones striking the nose section and fuel tanks respectively. (Source: @UkraineNow/82704)

Nationwide protests erupted in support of dismissed Defense Minister Fedorov, with demonstrations in Kyiv outside the Presidential Office, and in Lviv, Dnipro, Poltava, Lutsk, and Zaporizhzhia featuring anthem singing and demands for his reinstatement. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31662)

The Verkhovna Rada appointed Serhiy Koretskyi as new Prime Minister, while President Zelenskyy tasked Yevhen Khmar with performing Defense Minister duties pending permanent appointment. (Source: @UkraineNow/82709)
Ukraine received 501 bodies of fallen servicemen from Russia under a repatriation agreement, with law enforcement and forensic experts beginning identification procedures. (Source: @UkraineNow/82699)

Deputy Commander of the Ukrainian Air Force Pavlo Yelizarov resigned in protest over Fedorov's dismissal, stating the decision constitutes "great evil for Ukraine's defense capability." (Source: @DeepStateUA/23653)

Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga declared Ukraine ready for a Zelenskyy-Putin meeting in Turkey, citing strengthened battlefield position and successful asymmetric operations on Russian territory. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31683)
Russian forces launched Kh-59 cruise missiles at Odesa from tactical aviation, with at least two missiles confirmed targeting the city. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69103)

Multiple Shahed-type guided jet drones attacked Poltava, with reports of two drones initially and subsequent single drone approaching Shevchenkivskyi and Podilskyi districts. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69110)
Russian ballistic missile launches detected from Bryansk region, with four missiles reported and air defense systems engaged. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69120)
Russian aviation struck Zaporizhzhia with three KAB guided bombs, killing three civilians, damaging residential and non-residential buildings, and causing fires. (Source: @UkraineNow/82703)
Russian strikes hit civilian infrastructure in Kharkiv (one killed, five injured), Odesa (one killed, two hospitalized), and Dnipro (logistics warehouses damaged). (Source: @UkraineNow/82706)
Russian air defense units claimed destruction of 37 Ukrainian UAVs during a massive overnight raid, according to a "Lis" interceptor crew commander. (Source: @tass_agency/385612)
Russian Ministry of Defense reported strikes on port infrastructure and fuel storage tanks in Odesa port used to supply Ukrainian forces. (Source: @tass_agency/385623)
DeepState map update indicates Russian forces advanced near Ivanopil in Donetsk region. (Source: @DeepStateUA/23658)
Russian forces destroyed Ukrainian fortifications in settlements of Kramatorsk district, per Russian Ministry of Defense video release. (Source: @tass_agency/385605)
A Nova Poshta branch in Kramatorsk was struck by a KAB guided bomb, causing significant damage. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31676)
Russian tactical aviation activity reported on southern front with threat of air strikes on frontline areas. (Source: @kpszsu/68812)
Ballistic missile threat declared from northern direction, with launches confirmed from Bryansk region. (Source: @kpszsu/68815)
Drone activity detected in Chernihiv region: two jet drones flying along border toward Dobryanka. (Source: @eRadarrua/101306)
Drone activity in Sumy region: UAV southwest of Shostka heading toward Voronezh region of Russia. (Source: @kpszsu/68839)
Repeated missile launches from Bryansk region tracked, with air defense systems engaged. (Source: @eRadarrua/101339)
Jet-powered drones launched from Black Sea toward Odesa region. (Source: @kpszsu/68846)
Drone activity detected in Zaporizhzhia region: two UAVs toward Vilniansk from Ternuvate. (Source: @eRadarrua/101306)
Russian forces struck port infrastructure and fuel reservoirs in Odesa port used for Ukrainian military supply. (Source: @tass_agency/385623)
Russia banned imports of Turkish peaches after Turkey announced readiness to join security guarantees for Ukraine and lead maritime component with NATO allies. (Source: @UkraineNow/82711)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces are conducting a sustained multi-axis air campaign combining cruise missiles, ballistic missiles, and guided drones against Ukrainian rear areas, indicating improved coordination and intelligence. The simultaneous strikes on Odesa, Poltava, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, and Dnipro demonstrate expanded targeting capacity. Ukrainian asymmetric operations, including the Crimea airfield attack, show growing long-range strike capability. Political instability from Fedorov's dismissal risks degrading command cohesion at a critical juncture.
sections.regional_response: The United Kingdom's €300 million commitment for Gripen fighters signals sustained Western military support despite political transitions. Turkey's willingness to join security guarantees and lead a maritime component with NATO represents a significant Black Sea posture shift, prompting Russian economic retaliation. Hungary's investigation into former Foreign Minister Szijjarto's Russia ties reflects growing EU scrutiny of pro-Russian narratives. African operations cited by Russia suggest expanding geographic scope of proxy confrontation.
sections.intelligence_notes: The Bryansk launch site remains a persistent ballistic missile threat to northern and central Ukraine. Shahed drone attacks on Poltava indicate continued Russian focus on degrading Ukrainian logistics and command centers deep in rear areas. The Su-24M destruction in Crimea demonstrates Ukrainian naval special forces' growing reach. Protests across six major Ukrainian cities over Fedorov's dismissal reveal deep institutional friction. The 501-body repatriation suggests ongoing high-intensity combat losses. DeepState's Ivanopil advance confirmation indicates incremental Russian territorial gains in Donetsk.
